lesson.title: Measuring turns

lead.text: Turn on the spot until you face the way you started. That is a full turn. We cut it into 360 tiny equal turns called degrees (°).
Half a turn is a straight line. A quarter-turn is the corner of a page, called a right angle.
A full turn is 360° and a half-turn is 180°.

steps.headline: An angle measures a turn, and a full turn is 360°.

lead.text: A ray splits the corner of a page into two angles. Between them the two angles fill the whole right angle.

reveal.text: You took the part you knew from the whole corner. Angles that fill a corner always add to 90°.

steps.headline: A straight line is split into two angles. One is 41°. Find the other.

workedSteps.text: A straight line is a half-turn, 180°. The two angles fill it.

steps.headline: Two angles on a straight line. One is 68°. Find the other.

lead.text: A full turn takes you all the way round. A pointer that stops part of the way still has some turn left.

reveal.text: A full turn is 360°. You took the 140° already made from it, as you took a part from 90° and from 180°.

lead.text: Picture a door swinging open from closed. Is how far it has swung decided by how wide the door is?

lesson.orientation: Use quarter, half and full turns to find an unknown angle.
lesson.nextAction: Try the next idea, then return for a fresh problem after a delay.

blocks.text: A skater spins half a turn, then another quarter-turn. She wants to finish facing the way she started.

intro.promise: By the end you'll measure turns in degrees and find an unknown angle in a corner, on a line and round a point.

recap.keyIdea: An angle measures a turn. Parts of a right angle add to 90°, on a straight line to 180°, round a point to 360°.

blocks.text: You worked out that a skater who has made half a turn and a quarter-turn needs 1 more quarter-turn.
You found 112° beside 68° on a line, and 220° left of a full turn after 140°.

recap.nextHook: Three angles fill a straight line in a triangle too. Find out how they add up inside one.

questions.prompt: A 90° corner contains a 35° angle. How many degrees remain?
hints: Identify the total turn of the corner.
Subtract the known part from the total.
Calculate 90 − 35.
questions.onCorrect: The two parts fill the corner, so they add to 90°. Take the part you know from the whole.

misconceptions.feedback: 35° is the part you were given. The question asks for the part that is left.
That adds the 35° to the corner. The two parts together make the corner, not more.

questions.prompt: Two adjacent angles form a straight line. One is 68°. What is the other, in degrees?
hints: A straight line represents a half-turn.
The adjacent angles add to 180°.
Calculate 180 − 68.
questions.onCorrect: The other angle is 180° − 68° = 112°: the two angles fill the half-turn.

misconceptions.feedback: 68° is the angle you were given. Find the part that is left.
That adds 180 to 68. The whole is 180°, so the other part is smaller than that.

questions.prompt: A pointer has turned 140°. How many more degrees complete a full 360° turn in the same direction?
hints: Use a full turn as the total.
Find the turn that has not yet been made.
Calculate 360 − 140.
questions.onCorrect: 220°. The turn so far and the turn left make a full 360°.

misconceptions.feedback: 140° is the turn already made. Find the part still to come.
That is 180 − 140. A full turn is 360°, not 180°.

questions.prompt: The arms of an angle are drawn twice as long, along the same lines. What happens to its size in degrees?
hints: Separate the length of a ray from its direction.

answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: The degree measure depends on the directions of the rays, so extending them leaves the angle unchanged.

questions.onCorrect: The angle stays the same. It measures how far you turn, not how long the arms are.

misconceptions.feedback: A longer arm covers more paper, not more turn. The directions of the arms haven't changed.
Nothing was cut. The arms point the same way, so the turn is the same.

questions.prompt: A right angle is split into 27° and another angle. Find the other angle in degrees.
hints: A right angle is the whole.
Subtract the part already given.
Calculate 90 − 27.
questions.onCorrect: 63°. The parts of a right angle add to 90°, so subtract the part you know.

misconceptions.feedback: 117° comes from starting at 180°. A right angle is a quarter-turn, so start from 90°.
27° is the part you were given. Find the other part.

questions.prompt: Which pair can form a straight angle?
hints: Add each pair and compare with a half-turn.

answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: 72° + 108° = 180°, the measure of a straight angle.

questions.onCorrect: 72° + 108° = 180°. Two angles on a straight line fill a half-turn.

misconceptions.feedback: Those add to 90°, a right angle. A straight angle is a half-turn.
Those add to more than a half-turn: 190°.

questions.prompt: How many more quarter-turns bring her back to facing the way she started?
hints: How many quarter-turns make one whole turn?
A half-turn is two quarter-turns. How many has she made so far?
Take the quarter-turns she has made from the number in a whole turn.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: Half a turn is 2 quarter-turns, plus 1 more is 3. A whole turn is 4, so 1 more is needed.

questions.onCorrect: 1. A whole turn is 4 quarter-turns, and she has made 3. Angles measure how much of a turn has happened.

misconceptions.feedback: That's a whole turn from the start. She has already made some of it.
That's the half-turn she has made. Count the extra quarter-turn too.

questions.prompt: How many degrees is a right angle?
hints: A right angle is one quarter of a full turn.
How many degrees is a full turn?
Share 360° into four equal parts.
questions.onCorrect: 90°. A right angle is a quarter of 360°, the corner of a page.

misconceptions.feedback: 180° is a half-turn, a straight line. A right angle is half of that.
45° is an eighth of a turn. A right angle is a quarter.

questions.prompt: Why do the two angles add to 180°?
hints: What fraction of a turn is a straight line?

acceptedIdeas: Together they fill a half-turn, and a straight line is a half-turn.
answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: Together they fill a half-turn, and a straight line is a half-turn.

choices.label: Together they fill a half-turn, and a straight line is a half-turn.
Every pair of angles adds to 180°.
Because 180° is the size of a right angle.

questions.onCorrect: Two angles on a straight line fill a half-turn, so they add to 180°.

misconceptions.feedback: Only angles that fill a straight line do. A corner's parts add to 90°.
A right angle is 90°. A straight line is twice that.

questions.prompt: Three angles meet at a point and fill the whole turn. Two of them are 100° and 150°. What is the third, in degrees?
hints: What is the total of all three angles round a point?
Add the two angles you know.
Take that sum from the total.
questions.onCorrect: 110°. Angles round a point fill a full turn, so they add to 360°.

misconceptions.feedback: 250° is the two angles added together. The third angle is what is left of the turn.
That is 180 − 100. Round a point the total is 360°, not 180°.
